header: L6 · The test architect who has seen coverage lie · sonnet
verdict: The round-14 write pass mostly meets the lens (every new case but two names a removal), with one Required gap: the cause written when an interrupted changed-fingerprint salvage is resumed from salvaging is untested and decided two ways.

prior_resolution_notes.L6-r14-1: resolved as stated: RJ-338 states the row, a resume writes no entry, I17 gains the reset case with its removal; residue in L6-r15-1 and -2
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r14-2: resolved in part: first-salvage cause and a standalone-salvage case added, but the case does not isolate the standalone salvage (L6-r15-2)
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r14-3: resolved as stated: item g lists expected answers per try and the not-narrowed rule; trigger wording in L6-r15-3
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r14-4: resolved in part: per-target listing and dotless removal named; GOARCH not covered (L6-r15-4)
prior_resolution_notes.L6-r14-5: resolved in part: id-mismatch fixture added; the one-reader removal has no mechanism (L6-r15-5)

findings.defect: The cause of a salvage rerun resumed from salvaging after an interrupted fingerprint-changed salvage is decided two ways, and no I17 case asserts it.
findings.scenario: A changed-fingerprint salvage is killed or interrupted; 01 1.6 sends salvaging to salvaging with a new salvage id, and 3.8 enumerates 'rm ... from open or salvaging' as requested, so the row restarts at zero. A writer plus a Ctrl-C then escapes fingerprint-unstable. The definition 'a changed fingerprint started' reads the other way. The fault-injection case asserts convergence, never the cause.
findings.change: Say in 3.8 which cause a resume from salvaging writes (recommended: requested ends the row, stated as a rule, or fingerprint-changed if the interrupted entry was started by one), and add to I17 the case 'kill during a fingerprint-changed salvage, rerun' with the cause and the exit it must give; the removal that turns it red is the other choice. Cost: one sentence and one E case. Reaches the salvage tasks that build the rerun from 03 3.8 and I17 and T008 (error table).
findings.evidence: 03-formats.md:483 'requested for an entry a command writes on its own run, that is salvage ..., rm, recreate or retire from open or salvaging'; 01-system-model.md:304 'salvaging | ... starts the sandbox half again (the earlier command was interrupted or failed) | salvaging | new salvage id'; 05-security.md:172 (I17) fault injection asserts only 'converges'.

findings.defect: The case that a requested entry ends the row cannot tell a standalone salvage from the rm that follows it.
findings.scenario: The case 'a generation back at open ... a standalone salvage records requested, and the changed-fingerprint salvages of a later rm count from it' stays green if a standalone salvage does not end the row, because the later rm from open writes its own requested entry.
findings.change: Make the case end with a standalone salvage that succeeds and leaves the generation open with no later rm entry in between, or add a variant where the standalone salvage is the only requested entry after the changed ones; name the removal 'standalone salvage not ending the row'. Cost: one E case.
findings.evidence: 05-security.md:172 'a standalone salvage records requested, and the changed-fingerprint salvages of a later rm count from it'; 03-formats.md:483 rm from open writes requested.

findings.defect: The four Deferred rows' trigger is 'the dated entry ... records it', but item g allows an entry that says the token is not narrowed, so the trigger as written fires on any entry.
findings.scenario: The maintainer records an entry whose reads show Administration or a GitHub key; the rows read 'narrowed, as the dated entry records it' and reopen though the verdict is not narrowed.
findings.change: Word the trigger as 'an entry of item g whose verdict is narrowed (the note's closing rule)'. Cost: one clause in four rows and the token-narrowing row.
findings.evidence: 10-testing-style.md:916-921 'The entry is the event ... An A16 read that shows more than this repository ... means the token is not narrowed, and the entry says so'; spec.md Deferred rows 'the token is narrowed, as the dated entry of 10 10.2, item g, records it'.

findings.defect: The build-constraint fixture covers a GOOS difference only, while the lint targets also differ by GOARCH.
findings.scenario: An import behind an arm64-only tag is outside the approvals globs; listing linux and darwin on amd64 only still passes the fixture and the imports test.
findings.change: Add a fixture whose outside import builds only for arm64 and name its removal (listing one GOARCH per GOOS). Cost: one fixture.
findings.evidence: plan.md:565-578 'a fixture whose outside import builds only for darwin, whose removal is listing one target'; 10-testing-style.md:426 'linux and darwin, each on amd64 and arm64'.

findings.defect: The one-reader branch says 'a second reader inlined in either turns it red' but names no mechanism that can see an inlined reader.
findings.scenario: A test asserting 'both call the one reader' sees only calls; a second reader written as a direct yaml.Unmarshal in the generator is not a call to anything named, so the test stays green.
findings.change: Name the mechanism: an AST or import scan that fails when either consumer imports the YAML package or opens the file outside the reader's package, with a fixture for it. Cost: one small scan test.
findings.evidence: plan.md:590-599 'when T005 takes one reader, the test asserts that both call it, and a second reader inlined in either turns it red'.

findings.defect: The hint is conditional on whether a process is still writing, which romeu cannot know, so no test can assert the condition.
findings.scenario: The hint is a static string; a golden check sees both clauses and passes whichever branch the product 'meant'.
findings.change: Say in 04 4.4 that the hint is one fixed text naming both cases, so the golden test is on the whole string. Cost: one clause.
findings.evidence: 04-cli.md:326 'the hint says that a rerun with nothing written since this salvage resumes at sbx env rm, and, when a process is still writing that path, names the two recoveries'.

what_is_missing: A rule and case for the cause of a rerun resumed from salvaging; the verdict wording in the Deferred rows' trigger; a mechanism for the inlined-reader removal; a removal named for the excludeIgnored case.
postmortem: After v1.0.0 a user who interrupts a rerun is never paused by RJ-338 (01 1.6, 03 3.8, 04 4.4, I17); the four Deferred rows reopen on an entry that records 'not narrowed' (10 10.2 g, spec.md); an import behind an arm64-only tag escapes the approvals test (T005 b).
lens_critique: The lens asks whether a removal turns a test red but not whether the case reaches the branch it names: two cases here (the standalone salvage, the inlined reader) name a removal that cannot flip them. Success should also include states a crash can leave behind.
out_of_scope: Bullets on fake sbx fidelity, 80% per package, goldens, probes and the race run touch no changed text; 10 whole, 11 and S2 to S9 were not re-read. The S6 bullet (guard removal) was applied to the new I17 and T005 cases.
